If a resident cannot be located, the Nurse in charge of the area shall be responsible for notifying the Administrator and page overhead “Code_____ .” This will alert all staff that a resident is missing. Immediate attempts shall be made to determine where the resident was last seen and what the resident was wearing. Upon hearing a “CODE ___________ ,” do the following:

annotations.anchor_text: If Building Lockdown is ordered, observe exit and stairwell doors in your assigned work area.

Staff assigned to search outside should check areas behind shrubbery, bus stops, parked cars, etc. Staff searching at night should carry a flashlight and a means of communicating with the Command Center (radio , cell phone, etc.). During cold weather, staff should also carry a blanket for the resident. A picture of the missing resident should be provided to search teams, if available.

annotations.anchor_text: Staff assigned to search outside should check areas behind shrubbery, bus stops, parked cars, etc. Staff searching at night should carry a flashlight and a means of communicating with the Command Center (radio , cell phone, etc.). During cold weather, staff should also carry a blanket for the resident. A picture of the missing resident should be provided to search teams, if available.

NOTE : Factors such as the resident ’s condition and past history, time of day, weather conditions, etc. should be taken into consideration when deciding when to notify outside authorities. However, 30 minutes should be considered the maximum length of time allowed to elapse from the time that the resident was determined missing to the time the outside authorities are notified.

annotations.instruction_text: This plan is specific to New York State. Use Emerging Infectious Disease Response Plan (Part 1 – Section E) for clients outside of NYS.
annotations.anchor_text: PANDEMIC EMERGENCY PLAN

The facility will maintain or have access to a two (2) month supply of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). This supply of PPE with either be stored onsite or will be readily accessible by the facility.

As part of the Emergency Preparedness Program (EPP), the facility will maintain, or have readily accessible, a two (2) month supply of personal protective equipment (PPE) or any superseding requirements under New York State Executive Orders and/or NYS DOH regulations governing PPE supply requirements executed during a specific disease outbreak or pandemic, including gowns/isolation gowns, face shields/eye protection, masks, assorted sizes of disposable N95 respirators or other appropriate respiratory barrier devices, and gloves, sanitizer, and disinfectants (meeting EPA guidance current at the time of the event).

Only authorized staff may direct the activation/deactivation of the Pandemic Emergency/ Emerging Infectious Disease Response Plan. The activation and notification process should be used in accordance with the Emergency Operations Plan. Staff authorized to initiate activation/deactivation include the:
